einzeiler: Why corporate leadership is trapped in a religious mania of lying about artificial…
kurzfassung: Corporates across the globe are caught in a wave of artificial intelligence hype, where executives and employees alike feel forced to fabricate success stories. Based on insights from consultant Nikhil Suresh, the essay highlights how fear of being labeled incompetent drives a culture of deceit. Ultimately, workers use AI as a superficial buzzword while true believers in power make decisions detached from operational reality.
stichpunkte: Neoclassical economic assumptions lead people to believe powerful executives who claim artificial intelligence changes everything.
Data wizard Nikhil Suresh reports on hundreds of corporate conversations revealing a total absence of successful enterprise AI projects.
Employees face termination or missed promotions unless they express religious devotion to the transformative power of AI.
Corporate leaders are easily hypnotized by software demos despite admitting the underlying tools are unreliable.
Workers engage in AI-washing by completing tasks manually while pretending automated systems did the work.
Powerful figures embrace chatbots because unlike human subordinates, automated tools never talk back or question foolish requests.
Skilled practitioners experience satisfaction using automation as centaurs on their own terms, distinct from top-down corporate mandates.

kapitel.titel: The Psychology of Corporate True Believers

clips.hook: What would happen if chatbots vanished tomorrow?
clips.text: National infrastructure and government ministries would operate without interruption if authorities forced companies to shut down their conversational chatbots immediately.

clips.hook: Zero percent success in a year and a half
clips.text: Consultants investigating enterprise adoption found a complete failure rate across all client projects over an eighteen-month period.

clips.hook: The notorious accuracy rate of Cortex
clips.text: Database add-on tools promoted by major vendors carry an official error rate of at least eight percent under optimal conditions.
Corporate heads of artificial intelligence privately admit their positions are entirely meaningless while serving as the only remaining path to promotion.

clips.hook: AI is the asbestos of our technological society
clips.text: Modern organizations are actively embedding flawed automated systems into their foundational structures, creating hazards that future generations will spend decades removing.

beschreibung:
This week on my podcast, I read Why businesses lie about AI, a recent essay from my Pluralistic newsletter that breaks down Nikhil Suresh’s essay describing the total absence of any proof that any business is benefiting from AI deployment.

One person who’s had a lot of opportunity to observe the shear between the stated business/AI situation and the real business AI situation is Nikhil Suresh from Hermit Tech, a consulting firm of “radically ethical data wizards” (that is, tech consultants). Suresh reports on his experience talking with hundreds of executives (and, more importantly, their subordinates) about what (if anything) AI is doing for business in an essay entitled “AI Mania Is Eviscerating Global Decisionmaking.”
